headline: Risk-off day as AI slowdown warning and oil spike collide
body: Futures pointed sharply lower Monday after Anthropic's and OpenAI's chief executives published warnings calling for a deliberate slowdown in frontier AI development, a message that landed squarely on the AI-infrastructure trade that has driven much of this year's index gains. Nasdaq-100 futures fell roughly 1.8%, chip names led the declines, and the selloff spread from Asia — where a major AI-linked investor's shares dropped more than 10% — into U.S. premarket trading. The pullback compounds an already jittery macro backdrop: Brent crude jumped about 3% toward $108 a barrel after Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline stayed offline following drone attacks tied to the wider Middle East conflict, and traders are now pricing better-than-coin-flip odds of a Fed rate hike at Wednesday's meeting following Friday's hotter-than-expected inflation print. The VIX rose more than 11% intraday, consistent with a genuine volatility-of-concern move rather than an orderly dip.

The internals argue for a targeted unwind rather than blanket panic: gold actually slipped nearly 2% even as haven demand might normally lift it, hinting the move owes as much to rate repricing as to fear, while bitcoin held up with modest gains — a split that would be unusual in a true broad-based flight to safety. Retail-sentiment channels didn't surface much that was distinct from the day's headline story; trending-ticker trackers pointed mainly to the same AI and chip names already dominating the news rather than any separate social-media narrative, so today's read leans more on price action and the AI-slowdown/oil-price combination than on fresh crowd positioning. Barring further escalation in the Middle East or a surprise from the Fed, this looks more like a sentiment gut-check concentrated in AI-heavy names than a broader regime shift.
